weeks.weekly_summary: Establish aerobic base with 4 runs across the week. Focus on easy-paced running to build foundational fitness. Recent Strava data shows 2 runs in 14 days; ramping up to sustainable 4 runs/week at 7.0 hrs budget.
weeks.coaching_notes: Athlete has limited recent running volume (12.5 km in 14 days). Week 1 establishes a conservative base at ~38 km to avoid overtraining. Two quality sessions (one tempo, one short interval) introduce structured intensity while maintaining 80/20 polarization. All easy runs at 7:03/km (current fitness); tempo work at 6:12/km (current tempo pace). Recovery days are true rest or very easy strides only.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 2 increases to ~42 km (+9%) with slightly longer long run (16 km) and maintained quality structure. Tempo and intervals both present to develop aerobic threshold.

days.title: Easy 8km
days.description: Conversational pace aerobic building. Target 7:03/km. Flat route if possible to focus on cadence and relaxation.
days.notes: First run of block—establish rhythm and feel for easy pace.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Complete rest or mobility/stretching only.

days.title: Tempo Run 4km @ 6:12/km + Strides
days.description: 2km easy warm-up (7:03/km) → 4km tempo at 6:12/km (lactate threshold effort, challenging but sustainable) → 2km easy cool-down (7:03/km) → 6 × 100m strides on grass or track (90s walk recovery between).
days.notes: First quality session of block. Tempo pace is current proven fitness; should feel 'comfortably hard'. Strides reinforce leg turnover without excessive fatigue.

days.title: Long Run 14km Easy
days.description: Steady, conversational effort at 7:03/km. Build time-on-feet for marathon fitness. Fuel lightly (water every 2 km if >90 min). Focus on breathing rhythm and relaxation.
days.notes: Week 1 long run establishes baseline. No marathon-pace segments yet; pure aerobic base building.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Complete rest or easy yoga/mobility.

days.title: Interval Repeats: 5 × 1km @ ~6:12/km + Recovery
days.description: 1.5km easy warm-up (7:03/km) → 5 × 1km at 6:12/km with 90s easy jog recovery (7:30/km) → 1km easy cool-down (7:03/km). Goal: develop aerobic power while building lactate tolerance.
days.notes: Second quality session of week 1. 1km repeats are manageable and build neuromuscular fitness. Recovery jogs are crucial—do not skip.

days.title: Easy 7km
days.description: Relaxed aerobic running at 7:03/km. Day after quality—focus on easy movement and blood flow. Can be slightly slower if legs feel heavy.
days.notes: Low-stress run to flush out fatigue from Tuesday's intervals.

weeks.weekly_summary: Progressive aerobic development with 4 runs. Volume increases 9% to 42 km. Long run extends to 16 km (cumulative aerobic stimulus). Two quality sessions maintain polarization: tempo focus builds threshold power.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 2 ramps volume appropriately while respecting 10% rule (38.5 → 42 km = +9%). Long run grows from 14 to 16 km (1.5 km increase). Hard sessions stay at 2 per week, spread Thu/Sat (not consecutive). Athlete's recent Strava pace (7:03 easy, 6:12 tempo) is used consistently; no jump to faster paces needed yet—focus is volume and consistency.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 3 builds to ~44 km (+5%) with extended long run (17–18 km). Tempo and interval mix continues; intensity slightly elevated as aerobic base solidifies.

days.title: Tempo Run 5km @ 6:12/km
days.description: 2km easy warm-up (7:03/km) → 5km tempo at 6:12/km (1 min faster than easy pace; focus on holding effort) → 2km easy cool-down (7:03/km) → 4 × 100m strides.
days.notes: Tempo distance increased 1km from Week 1 (4→5km). Athlete should feel strong but not desperate. Pace locked at 6:12/km per current fitness.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Complete rest.

days.title: Easy 8km
days.description: Steady aerobic run at 7:03/km, day after tempo. Can be slightly easier if needed; focus is aerobic continuation, not pace.
days.notes: Day before long run—keep easy to preserve energy.

days.title: Long Run 16km Easy
days.description: Conversational pace at 7:03/km. 16km builds aerobic stamina and mental resilience for marathon training. Refuel at 45–60 min mark if carrying gels/water. Focus on relaxation and breathing.
days.notes: Long run grows to 16km (2km increase from Week 1). Athlete should feel controlled effort; finish strong but not depleted.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Recovery day following long run.

days.title: Interval Repeats: 6 × 800m @ ~6:12/km with Recovery
days.description: 1.5km easy warm-up (7:03/km) → 6 × 800m at ~6:12/km with 90s easy jog recovery (7:30/km) → 1km easy cool-down (7:03/km). Develop aerobic speed and leg strength.
days.notes: Interval session progresses from 5 × 1km (Week 1) to 6 × 800m. Shorter repeats allow slightly faster pace perception while building intensity capacity.

days.title: Easy 7km
days.description: Relaxed recovery run at 7:03/km, day after intervals. Very conversational; focus on flushing legs and enjoying the movement.

weeks.weekly_summary: Peak week of block: 4 runs totaling 44 km (+5% vs Week 2). Long run extends to 18 km. Quality sessions include longer tempo and tempo-intervals to transition toward marathon-pace work. Maintain 80/20 polarization.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 3 is the highest-volume week in the block (44 km). Long run reaches 18 km, preparing for extended marathon-specific efforts ahead. Tempo work increases to 6km; intervals shift toward 1km repeats again (neuromotor variety). Quality sessions remain spaced (Thu/Tue) to avoid consecutive hard days. Athlete's paces locked at 7:03 easy, 6:12 threshold—no acceleration yet; focus is volume consistency and aerobic power development.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 4 is recovery week: volume drops 20% to ~35 km. Long run cut to 14–15 km. One quality session (tempo or short intervals) maintains stimulus while allowing physiological adaptation.

days.title: Tempo Run 6km @ 6:12/km + Strides
days.description: 2km easy warm-up (7:03/km) → 6km tempo at 6:12/km (hold sustainable hard effort across full 6km; mental challenge) → 2km easy cool-down (7:03/km) → 6 × 100m strides.
days.notes: Tempo distance reaches 6km. This is a significant session—6km at threshold is aerobic-demanding. Athlete should feel strong but controlled. If breathing is ragged, dial back slightly and finish the reps.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Complete rest or very light mobility.

days.title: Easy 8km
days.description: Steady aerobic run at 7:03/km. Day before long run—keep relaxed and easy to preserve glycogen and energy.
days.notes: Easy day before peak long run. Stay controlled.

days.title: Long Run 18km Easy
days.description: Extended aerobic run at 7:03/km. 18km is peak distance for this block, building significant marathon stamina. Fuel every 45 min (gels/sports drink), hydrate consistently. Relax shoulders, control breathing, enjoy the fitness.
days.notes: Week 3 long run peak at 18km. Athlete is now building genuine marathon aerobic capacity. Finish strong; this is a confidence builder.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Recovery day following long run.

days.title: Interval Repeats: 5 × 1km @ 6:12/km with 90s Recovery
days.description: 1.5km easy warm-up (7:03/km) → 5 × 1km at 6:12/km with 90s easy jog recovery (7:30/km) → 1km easy cool-down (7:03/km). Build aerobic speed and mental toughness.
days.notes: Return to 1km repeats (from Week 2's 800m). Longer intervals allow greater aerobic stimulus and rhythm establishment. Pace locked at 6:12/km—this is current proven fitness.

days.title: Easy 6km
days.description: Short, relaxed recovery run at 7:03/km, day after intervals. Light effort; focus on movement and flushing.
days.notes: Intentionally short day to manage fatigue before recovery week.

weeks.weekly_summary: Recovery week: volume drops 20% to 35 km. Long run reduced to 14km. One quality session (short tempo) maintains intensity while allowing supercompensation. Easy running dominates. Prepare for Aerobic Development phase in next block.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 4 is mandatory recovery (−20% volume: 44 → 35 km). Long run cut from 18 to 14 km (−20%). One quality session (4km tempo on Thursday) sustains threshold stimulus without overloading. Remaining days are easy runs (7:03/km) and rest. This week allows accumulated fatigue to dissipate and triggers adaptation gains. Athletes often feel slow/sluggish early in recovery week—this is normal. Energy and aerobic power typically surge the following week.
weeks.next_week_preview: Next 4-week block (Week 5+) enters Aerobic Development phase: volume ramps back up; long runs extend to 20–22 km; marathon-pace segments introduced in long runs. Quality sessions shift toward tempo-intervals and progression runs.

days.title: Tempo Run 4km @ 6:12/km
days.description: 2km easy warm-up (7:03/km) → 4km tempo at 6:12/km (back to Week 1 distance; focus is maintenance, not progression) → 2km easy cool-down (7:03/km) → 3 × 100m strides.
days.notes: Recovery week: tempo distance drops back to 4km. Goal is to maintain threshold fitness without excessive fatigue. Athlete should feel fresher than Week 3; pace still 6:12/km.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Complete rest.

days.title: Easy 7km
days.description: Relaxed aerobic run at 7:03/km, day before long run. Very conversational; no pressure on pace.

days.title: Long Run 14km Easy
days.description: Easy-paced long run at 7:03/km. Reduced from 18km to 14km (recovery week). Still builds endurance but at lower cumulative stress. Focus on relaxation and enjoying the run.
days.notes: Long run cut 20% (18 → 14 km). Athlete should feel noticeably fresher than Week 3. Finish energized, not depleted.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Recovery following long run.

days.title: Easy 5km
days.description: Short, very easy run at 7:03/km (or slower if legs feel heavy). Recovery week philosophy: low-stress movement. Can walk portions if needed.
days.notes: Intentionally short and easy to finish week gently.

days.title: Rest Day
days.description: Complete rest. End recovery week fully recharged.

roadmap.weekly_summary: Volume ramps back up to 48km after recovery week. Long run extends to 20km; two quality sessions maintain threshold and VO2max. Transition toward marathon-pace segments and extended aerobic efforts.

Volume continues building to 51km. Long run introduces marathon-pace segments (first MP work). Quality session shifts to tempo-intervals (cruise repeats). Athlete bridges from pure aerobic to marathon-specific pacing.
Peak aerobic week at 53km. Long run extends to 22km with significant MP work. Fartlek session develops lactate tolerance. Athlete is now building peak aerobic power and marathon-specific endurance.
Recovery week before Peak Training block. Volume drops 20% to 42km. Long run 18km (easy pace). One quality session maintained. Allows adaptation before high-intensity Peak Training phase.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes aerobic foundation and introduces structured quality work. Week 1 (38.5 km) conservatively establishes base load from recent Strava data (12.5 km in 14 days). Weeks 2–3 ramp progressively (+9%, +5%) to 44 km peak, growing long run from 14 to 18 km. Week 4 recovery (35 km, −20%) allows supercompensation. All paces anchored to current verified fitness: easy 7:03/km, tempo 6:12/km. Two quality sessions per week (tempo + intervals) maintain 20% hard-intensity stimulus while respecting 80/20 polarization. No hard sessions on consecutive days; spacing respects recovery. Athlete transitions into Aerobic Development phase (Week 5+) with elevated volume, marathon-pace introduction, and longer aerobic outputs. By end of next 4-week block, athlete will be primed for Peak Training and marathon-specific efforts.
